services.name: AI assistants on your documents
services.promise: A chatbot that answers questions using your own manuals, policies or product information, and says so when it doesn't know.
needIf: Your team or customers ask the same questions again and again
Important answers are buried in long documents
You want AI help without sending everything to a generic chatbot
youGet: An assistant that answers from your documents and shows where each answer came from
Guardrails so it stays on topic and admits when it isn't sure
A simple way to update the documents it uses
Documentation and a hand-over session
steps: Agree on what the assistant should and shouldn't answer
Collect and review the documents it will learn from
Build a first version and test it with real questions
Review the answers together and tune it
Add it where your users are (website, internal tool)
Hand over with documentation and training

services.name: Dashboards and automated reports
services.promise: One live dashboard instead of rebuilding the same spreadsheet every week.
needIf: Someone spends hours every week preparing the same report
Numbers from different systems never quite match
You make decisions on gut feeling because the data is hard to see
youGet: A dashboard connected to your data that refreshes automatically
Clear definitions for every number on it
Checks that flag when the data looks wrong
A training session for your team
steps: Agree on the key numbers you want to track
Get access to your data and check its quality
Clean and connect the data
Build a first version and review it together
Refine it based on your feedback
Set up automatic refresh, then hand over with training
services.experience: Built and maintained 15+ Power BI dashboards and automated recurring reports as a data analyst at Coast Capital Savings, cutting manual work by 45%

A plain-English explanation of what drives the predictions
A simple way to use it: a list, a dashboard or a small tool
Notes on its limits and when to retrain it
steps: Agree on the question and what a useful answer looks like
Explore your data and check what it can and can't tell us
Build and compare several models fairly
Review the results and what drives them together
Turn the best model into something your team can use
Hand over with documentation and a plan for keeping it accurate

services.name: Automation and data extraction

needIf: Someone copies information from PDFs or websites into spreadsheets

Tests, documentation and a short training
steps: Walk me through the manual process you do today

Make it simple to run for your team
Hand over with instructions and a short training

Launch on your domain

process.title: How a project works
process.luffy: No surprises here. Every step ends with something you see and approve before the next one starts.

steps.name: Free discovery call
steps.what: We talk about the problem, your data or content, and what success looks like.
steps.checkpoint: We agree whether it's worth doing

steps.name: Written proposal
steps.what: Scope, steps, price, what's included and what isn't, and the timeline.
steps.checkpoint: You approve the proposal before any work starts

steps.name: Data and design check
steps.what: I look at your real data or content and confirm the plan works.
steps.checkpoint: "Go", or we adjust the plan together

steps.name: Build, step by step
steps.what: The work happens in small pieces, and I show you each one.

steps.name: Handover
steps.what: The final version, documentation and training for your team.

steps.name: Support
steps.what: I fix anything that doesn't work as we agreed.

timeline.title: When will it be done?
timeline.text: Every project is different, so I don't guess a timeline before I understand yours. After the free call and a look at your data, the written proposal includes a timeline for each step, which you approve before any work begins. If something changes along the way, I tell you straight away and we agree on a new plan together.
factors: How ready and clean your data or content is
How many systems or data sources are involved
How quickly feedback comes back at each checkpoint
Changes to the scope after the work starts

pricing.title: What will it cost?
pricing.text: Every project is priced individually after our first conversation, based on what you actually need. You'll get a clear written price in the proposal before any work starts, and any change is agreed in writing first, so there are no surprise bills.

promises.title: My promises to you
items: A written scope and price before any work starts
Something to see and approve at every step, and regular progress updates
You own everything: the code, data, accounts and documentation
Changes are agreed in writing first, so there are no surprise bills
Your data stays private, with an NDA on request, and I delete my copies after handover
If I'm not the right fit for your project, I'll say so and point you elsewhere

faq.q: Do I need to know anything technical?
faq.a: Not at all. I'll explain everything in plain language, and you only need to know your business and your goals.

faq.q: What if my data is messy?
faq.a: That's normal. The data and design check exists for exactly this: I look at your real data early and tell you honestly what's possible before the main work starts.
You do. The code, data, accounts and documentation are all yours at handover.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Ontario?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely with clients anywhere in Canada and the US, and I'm happy to meet in person around Kitchener-Waterloo.
After our first conversation. Every project is different, so you'll get a written price for your specific project in the proposal, before any work begins.
There's a support period to fix anything that doesn't work as agreed. After that, I'm happy to help with changes or improvements as a new piece of work.

planner.title: Plan my project
planner.luffy: Answer a few quick questions and I'll sketch the steps your project would go through.
